history.summary: IDENTITY UNVERIFIED: the CSV row names only 'Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple, Tumkur' with no address, and several famous Lakshmi Narasimha temples exist in Tumkur district (Devarayanadurga, Seebi, Vignasante) and just across the district line (Marehalli in Malavalli taluk, Mandya district). This file documents the Bhogalakshminarasimhaswamy temple at Devarayanadurga (Devarayana Durga hills, ~17 km from Tumkur city), the best-supported match for a Tumkur-area entry. It is the lower of the two Narasimha temples on the hill (Yoga Narasimha stands higher up). The temple is built in Dravidian style with garbhagriha, sukanasi, navaranga, mukhamantapa and porch, set in an enclosure with a mahadvara. The Karnataka archaeology department records that it was built by Kanthirava Narasaraja Wodeyar of Mysore and repaired in 1858 by Krishnaraja Wodeyar III. If the intended record was the 12th-century Marehalli temple or the 1286 CE Hoysala Vignasante temple, this file should be replaced.

name: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple
town_description: Devarayanadurga is a hill-station village about 17 km southeast of Tumkur city, set on rocky hills rising to roughly 3,940 feet. Named after the Mysore ruler Chikka Devaraja Wodeyar, it is a combined pilgrim and trekking destination, with the Bhoga Narasimha temple at the base of the climb and the Yoga Narasimha shrine higher up. A state-run medicinal-plant nursery with over 300 species of herbs operates nearby.

travel.road: ~17 km from Tumkur city via the Tumkur-Dobbaspete (NH-48/7526 corridor) hill road (verify)
